entries.doc: SECTION 1 - Compliance
entries.title: Safeguarding
entries.html:
Introduction

1The BHA Safeguarding requirements in relation to racecourses apply in relation to Industry personnel attending the racecourse in advance of, on, or following a race day, in connection with their race day duties.

2This BHAGI has been written in two parts. This first part covers mandatory minimum requirements. Annex A has been developed in conjunction with the Racecourse Association and is provided for be st practice guidance and to assist the Managing Executive in the development and implementation of policies relevant to their individual venue.

3In this BHAGI, all references to a “child" or “children" are references to an individual or individuals under the age of 18.

Racecourse Policy

4Each Racecourse shall prepare, implement, and regularly review written policies and procedures for the safeguarding of children and adults at risk. As a minimum, the policy must include:

a)a statement setting out the Raceco urse’s commitment to protecting all children and adults at risk;

b)what the Racecourse will do to keep children and adults at risk safe and respond to concerns;

c)a list of the supporting procedures that accompany the policy; and

d)reference to the B HA Safeguarding Policy and reporting processes available from the BHA website – click here*

*Note: Each racecourse policy must ma ke reference to the BHA Safeguarding Policy. I n the event of a conflict between the two policies the racecourse policy shall prevail.

Designated Safeguarding Lead

5Each Racecourse shall designate at least one senior member of staff with the necessary skills and expertise as its Designated Safeguar ding Lead (DSL). The name of the Racecourse DSL shall be included as a named person on the licence when an application for a licence is made.

6Where appropriate, the DSL may delegate any of their safeguardin g responsibilities to one or more other member s of staff (Deputy DSL). In such circumstances, the DSL must supervise the work of the Deputy DSL and ensure that they are properly trained, and supported BHAGI 1.5 Dtd 3 October 2022

7Each DSL and any Deputy DSL shall:

a)be DBS checked (to the highest level of check for which they are eligible);

b)be trained in the safeguarding of children and adults at risk, such training to be refreshed as appropriate;

c)be given a job description that properly records their responsibilities*.

*Note: further details are provided at Annex A of areas that should be included within the relevant job description

8The DSL and/or Deputy DSL shall be present and/or accessible for ever y race day, including when participants have booked to stay overnigh t ahead of the race day or for any other reaso n when participants may be required to stay overnight in relation racing activities. 9. In addition, clear sig nage providing the name and contact information should be displayed in the Overnight Accommodation, Stable Staff Canteen, Jockey Changing Rooms and Stewards Room. 10. Each DSL will maintain a training record wi th respect to safeguarding in line with applicable laws and government or local authority issued guidance.

Minimum Safeguarding Standards – Weighing Room

Safeguarding risk assessment and risk mitigation measures

11The DSL, Deputy DSL or another suffic iently informed member of staff must conduct a safeguarding risk assessment in respect of the weighing room and changing areas and identify and implement appropriate measures aimed at mitigating identified risks in order to creat e a safer environment for chil dren (i.e., those under the age of 18) and adults. The risk assessment and any resulting measures should be documented and regularly reviewed to ensure that it is up to date with current safeguarding legislatio n, guidance and specific facility usage demand s, including any necessary changes required, e.g., for specific meetings such as festivals or COVID-19 measures.

A copy of the risk assessme nt, and details o f any resultant measures, must be sent to the Racecourse Department as soon as completed and a reviewed document by 1 October annually thereafter.

Minimum requirements in relation to children’s changing area (under 18’s)

12The following safeguarding risk mitigation measures are required as a minimum from 4 January 2 022 (others may be ident ified through the risk assessment process above):

a)Within the male and female changing areas there must be a private changing area in which under 18’s can change, such as a cubicle, screened off area, or a designated changing room.

b)The under 18’s changing area must not be visible to the public. BHAGI 1.5 Dtd 3 October 2022

c)There m ust be a private shower cubicle available to under 18’s with a closing, lockable door in both male and female changing areas or a designated changing room.

d)Under 18’s must be advised to use the under 18’s changing and shower area when showering or fully changing clothes.

e)The use of cameras and other recording equipment is not permitted in the shower or changing areas.

75 High Holborn Circulation London Racecourse Association WC1V 6LS

Best Practice Guidance For Safeguarding Annex A

Annex A to BHAGI 1.5 Dtd 3 October 2022

BEST PRACTICE GUIDANCE FOR SAFEGUARDING

Key Principles

1The aim of the 'best practice' guida nce is to provide further information on the mandatory re quirements in BH AGI 1.4, including the Industry expectations. This is designed to assist the Managin g Executive in the production and implementation of a safeguarding policy which reflects the needs and obligations of their individual racecourse and the aims of the British Horseracing Industry to prov ide high standards of care for all children and adults at risk.

2These regulations apply when Industry personne l are attending a racecourse on or in advance of a race day as part of their race day duti es. Racecourses will also need to consider their re sponsibilities for racing staff who stay overnight at accommodation arranged, but not provided, by the racecourse.

3The legal responsibilities and du ty of care of racecourses in relation to their own staff, members of the public, and in relation to non -racing events, fall outside the requirements of the BH AGI. However, racecourses should ensure that they consider these when developing and implementing their individual safeguarding policies, including the circumstances when referral should be made to BHA . An y Safeguarding concerns involving a member of the BHA Raceday team or the racecourse staff (including but no t limited to raceday staff) should be notified to BHA in accordance with paragraphs 12 - 16 below.

4In addition to this best practice guidan ce, Managing Executives must comply with applicable laws and government or local authority issued guidance.

5This best practice guidance has been dev eloped by the BHA and Racecourse Association based on research, experience and Industry feedback.

6Any d eviations from this guidance should be necessary and reasonable and should achieve an equal or higher standar d. Such deviations should be recorded with written supporting material.

7Further prac tical advice and guid ance for racecourses is availab le fr om the Racecourse Association.

Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)

8BHAGI 1.4 requires each Racecourse to designate at least one senior member of staff as its Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL), with appointed Deputy /Deputies as appropriate. Each DSL must have a clear job description that properly r ecords their responsibilities. This should include:

a)leadership on safeguarding at the Racecourse;

b)ensure strict compliance with the Racecourse’s policies and procedures for the safeguarding of children and adults at risk;

c)review and approve the safeguarding measures for all racing activities that take place at the Racecourse; Annex A to BHAGI 1.5 Dtd 3 October 2022

d)Be the fi rst point of contact for any report, suspicion of ab use or concern relating to the welfare of children o r adult at risk engaged in racing activity at the Racecourse;

e)Be the lead Racecourse Official in any investigation of allegations of abuse of children or adult at risk, or other safeguarding concerns;

f)provide guidance to and support for any member of staff engaged in each activity who reports suspected abuse of children or adults at risk or concerns as to their welfare; and

g)be responsible for maintaining clear, comprehensive and up -to-date records of all reported allegations of concerns for the safety and/or wellbeing of a child or adult at risk.

9In addition, when undertaking their duties, the DSL should be gu ided by the advice of the relevant local and statutory authorities with regard t o issues concerning the safeguarding of children and adults at risk.

Weighing Room

10The following guidance also applies in respect of the weighing room and changing areas more generally, i.e., irrespective of the age of those using weighing room and changing areas:

a)Safeguarding material concernin g app ropriate use of the facilities should be displayed in the changing area.

b)Officials and anyone else other than Jockeys and Valets should not be accessing areas where Jockeys (of any age) are in a state of undress w ithout careful consideration of these safeg uarding standards. All Valets, Jo ckeys and anyone else requiring access to the weighing room and changing areas should have completed the BHA Introduction to Safeguarding in the Horseracing Industry online education programme.

c)Jockeys have been informed (as outlined in BHA/RCA guidan ce) that they should wear, for example, shorts, or, top and shorts, or, other sports clothing to cover up in between getting changed . Any f urther requirements i dentified following the racecourse specific risk assessment should be communicated by the DSL or nominated person.

d)Scales should be positione d so that Jockeys wishing to weigh themselv es “stripped” can do so in priv ate and away fro m others. If it is no t possible to move the scales to a private area in the short term, then racecourses should provide a screen around the scales to allow jockeys pr ivacy when requiring to weigh “stripped”.

Annex A to BHAGI 1.5 Dtd 3 October 2022

Racecourse Staff

11Each member of staff employed directly by the racecourse should be informed of:

a. the Racecourse Safeguarding Policy and an y ac companying guidance documents;

b. the contact details of the DSL and any Deputy DSL;

c. what const itutes poor safeguarding pract ice, ab use or un suitable behaviour towards a child or adult at risk; and

d. the re porting process in the event of a safe guarding concern being witnessed or suspected by them or reported to them.

12Racecourses must ensure that, in advance of a raceday, they confirm with any third party contractors that they have safeguarding policies and procedures in place where the activities of the third party contractors in question concern children or adults at risk in any way, or otherwise give rise to safeguarding considerations.

Notification of Referral to BHA

13On making any referral of concerns for the safety and/or wellbeing of child or adult at risk to any externa l agency (including, without limitation, the police, the local authority or the DBS), the DS L or other Official making the referral should consider whether it is appropriate to notify the BHA Lead Safegua rding Manager / Safeguarding Officer. This will ensure that the BHA Lead Safeguarding Manager / Safeguarding Offi cer is kept fully apprised of the progress of the referral and any subsequent investigation or action.

14Where necessary, and if specified by the police or ot her external authority , referrals to the BHA can be made on a no names ba sis. H owever, if the identity is withheld by the ra cecourse, consideration should be given as to how harm ma y be mitigated if the concern relates to an individual who continues to be involved in racing activities. The BHA Lead Safeguarding Manager / Safegua rding Officer should be made aware as soon a s reas onably practicable, and ideally within 24 hour s of the relevant evidence, incident or investigation being referred to the external agency ( where such a referral is made).

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: RACE PROGRAMMING POLICY (previously in Rules of Racing)
entries.html:
1All race programmes must comply with BHAGI 2.1 and any additional race programme policy issued by the Authority from time to time.

Conditions of Races

2The conditions of a race must meet the following requirements:

• the Maximum Figure for a race must not exceed the Safety Factor; • the number of horses permitted to start the race must not exceed either the Maximum Figure or the Safety Factor.

3The conditions of a race must not contain any restrictions as to training stables.

Minimum Requirements as to Races to be Included in a Flat Race Programme

4In each day’s programme of racing, there must be two races of a mile or upwards.

525% of races programmed must be at least a distance of ten furlongs or upwards per quarter.

6In addition, racecourses must achieve either the following:

• 10% of races programmed must be at least a distance of twelve furlongs or upwards per quarter; or • 6% of races programmed must be at least a distance of fourteen furlongs and upwards per quarter.

7From January 1st until the first Saturday in June, each fixture should include at least one type of Maiden, Novice or Conditions Race open to three year olds.

8Where the programme is held at or after the start of the week that follows the Doncaster St Leger Meeting but before the end of The Flat Season, the daily programme of races to be run must include at least one race of between six to eight furlongs restricted to Maiden or Novice two year olds.

9From the start of the Flat Season until the end of the year, each racecourse must stage 21.5% of their race programme as Maiden, Novice or Conditions Races per quarter. Additionally, there is a minimum requirement of one such race per daily programme.

10From January 1st to the day before the start of the Flat Season, each racecourse to stage one Maiden or Novice Race for every day’s racing. BHAGI 2.1 Dtd 28 March 2026

11Any fixture must consist of at least six programmed races and these must include, unless the Total Prize Fund exceeds £100,000 for that day, a minimum of two of those races potentially liable to division under Rule (I)9.

12For a programme of seven races, at least two races which are potentially liable to division must still be programmed albeit only one may be permitted to divide at the time determined in accordance with the Race Administration Code.

13The Authority shall seek the agreement of the Racecourse Managing Executive if, in exercise of its general powers, the BHA proposes to waive the application of paragraph 10 (above) for a particular meeting.

General Restrictions on Flat Races

14The Total Prize Fund of a Flat race may not be less than £4,300.

15Standard handicaps must have a 20lb weight-range.

16No flat race may be run over less distance than five furlongs. No flat race may be run over a distance in excess of two miles and six furlongs.

17No horse may run in any race before having reached the age of two.

18For the period starting on January 1st and ending on July 31st in any year, there must not be more than two flat races confined to two year olds in a programme of six races, or more than three such races in a programme of seven races.

19On or after August 1st in any year, there must not be more than three flat races confined to two year olds in any programme.

20Subject to paragraph 21 (below), no two year old may run before The Flat Season commences in any year:

• more than five furlongs until the Monday after the Newmarket Craven Meeting/Newbury Spring Trials (Greenham) Meeting, whichever is later, • more than six furlongs before the Saturday after the York Dante Meeting, • more than seven furlongs before August 1st, • more than nine furlongs before September, • in a Handicap Race before July 1st,

21No two year old which, in the period starting on July 1st and ending on December 31st in any year, was foaled in the southern hemisphere may run:

• before September 16th; • more than five furlongs before November 1st; • more than six furlongs, or in a Handicap Race, at any time.

22No three year old, which, in the period starting on July 1st and ending on December 31st in any year, was foaled in the southern hemisphere may run:

• more than seven furlongs before February 1st; BHAGI 2.1 Dtd 28 March 2026

• more than eight furlongs before March 1st; • more than nine furlongs before April 1st; • more than ten furlongs, or in a Handicap Race with older horses, before July 1st.

23No horse may carry more than 12st in a flat race. No account will be taken of:

• a jockey’s allowance claimed in accordance with the Weights and Handicapping Code, or • a weight allowance claimed in accordance with the conditions of a race.

24Only races confined to apprentice jockeys or amateur jockeys will be allowed to specify any jockeys’ allowances, outside of those provided for under Rule.

Minimum Requirements as to Races to be Included in a Jump Race Programme

25There must be at least one Steeple Chase in each day’s programme.

26For every two days programmed there must be at least three Novice or Maiden or Juvenile Weight­for­Age Hurdle Races, excluding Selling Races, Claiming Races and Novice Handicap Hurdle Races (excluding fixtures taking place from March to August – see para 29).

27For every day programmed from March to August, there must be at least one Novice or Maiden or Juvenile Weight -for-Age Hurdle Races, excluding Selling Races, Claiming Races and Novice Handicap Hurdle Races.

28For every three days programmed (apart from mixed meetings) there must also be at least

• one race restricted to Fillies and/or Mares only, and • one Novice or Maiden or Beginners’ Weight­for­Age Steeple Chase or one Novices’ Handicap Steeple Chase classified as Class 1, 2 or 3.

29For every four days programmed (apart from mixed meetings) there must also be at least one National Hunt Flat Race

30The programme of races must consist of at least six and no more than eight races except outside British Summer Time when there will be no more than seven races.

General Restrictions in Jump Racing

31No horse may run in:

• a hurdle race until May 1st of the year in which it is three years old, • a steeple chase until July 1st of the year in which it is four years old, or • a Hunters' Steeple Chase until January 1st of the year in which it is five years old.

32With effect from 1 April 2023, no horse may carry less than 10st 2lb in a hurdle race, steeple chase or National Hunt Flat Race unless:

• a jockey's allowance is claimed in accordance with the Weights and Handicapping Code, or • the race is confined to Conditional Jockeys, as provided in the conditions of the race.

33Only races confined to conditional jockeys will be allowed to specify any jockeys’ allowances, outside of those provided for under Rule.

34No steeple chase or hurdle race may be run over a distance of less than two miles.

35No horse may carry more than 13st in a steeple chase, hurdle race or National Hunt Flat Race. No account will be taken of:

• a jockey’s allowance claimed in accordance with the Weights and Handicapping Code or • a weight allowance claimed in accordance with the conditions of the race.

National Hunt Flat Race

36No horse may run in a National Hunt Flat Race

• unless the horse is trained by a Person who is authorised (whether by licence, permit or otherwise) to train for steeple chases, hurdle races and National Hunt Flat Races;

37The conditions of a National Hunt Flat Race must provide:

• that the race is a Weight-for-Age Race which

- is not less than one and a half miles, - is not more than two and a quarter miles, - is for horses which at starting have not run under any recognised Rules of flat racing, steeple chasing or hurdle racing, apart from in National Hunt Flat Races run under these Rules or in Irish National Hunt Flat Races or in French AQPS races.

• that any jockey must be one of the following

- a Conditional Jockey, - an Overseas Jockey whose authorisation by a Recognised Racing Authority corresponds to a Conditional Jockey's licence, - an Amateur Jockey who holds a Category B permit to ride granted by the Authority, - an Overseas Jockey whose authorisation by a Recognised Racing Authority corresponds to such a permit, and BHAGI 2.1 Dtd 28 March 2026

- if the race is deemed to be 'Open', a Jockey who holds a licence to ride in steeple chases, hurdle races or National Hunt Flat Races or an Overseas Jockey whose authorisation by a Recognised Racing Authority corresponds to such a licence.

Hunters’ Steeple Chases

38With regard to Hunters' Steeple Chases:

• no race may be run before January 1st of any season, and • the qualification in any race is limited to the particular period specified in the Hunters' Certificate.

Declarations to Run in Jump Races

39Deleted

Weight Allowances for Horses – All Races

40No weight allowance shall be made to any horse that is:

• the produce of a stallion or mare whose produce never won a race; • the first produce of a mare; • the produce of a stallion covering at, or under, a particular fee; or • a half-bred.

41The only circumstances under which a horse may be given a weight allowance or be relieved of extra weight because it has failed to win one or more races , are if the horse:

• is a Maiden; • has not won within a specified time; or • has not won races of a specified value or distance.

Selling and Claiming Races

Sale Price

42Where the Total Prize Fund is £6,000 or less, the selling price must not be less than £3,000.

43Where the Total Prize Fund is more than £6,000, the selling price must not be less than £4,000.

44In relation to a Selling Race, the commission retained by racecourses on the sale of any winning horse sold through the post-race auction, including those horses which are bought back by the existing trainer or owner, will be capped at 10% of the sale price. Racecourses do have the option to charge less than this if they wish. Details regarding the commission rate must be stated in the conditions of the race.

45In respect of the sale of the winner in a Selling Race, the racecourse must act as guarantor for the final selling price. . Advertised Claiming Price

46In relation to a Claiming Race:

• the maximum Advertised Claiming Price must not be less than the advertised Prize Money; and • the minimum Advertised Claiming Price must not be less than £2,000.

47In relation to a Selling Race, the Advertised Claiming Price must not be less than the advertised selling price of the winner.

48A weight allowance in accordance with the conditions of the race shall be included when the Owner is prepared to accept an Advertised Claiming Price below the maximum permissible Advertised Claiming Price laid down in the conditions of the race.

Holborn Gate Circulation 26 Southampton Buildings Stewards London Assistant Stewards WC2A 1AN Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: FIXTURE FEES AND PAYMENTS (previously in Rules of Racing)
entries.html:
FIXTURE FEES

1When a fixture takes place, the Racecourse Managing Executive must pay to the Authority: • fees of such amount as the Authority may from time to time decide; and • fees in respect of the receipt of entries.

2Unless the Authority directs otherwise, fees payable under paragraph 1 remain payable even if the fixture, or any part of it, is abandoned.

Date by which Payment to be Made

3Unless payment is requested earlier, the f ollowing sums must be paid to the Stakeholder within 7 days of the Race or, if the last day for payment falls on a weekend or public holiday in Great Britain, on the next business day:

• any Prize Money; • any payment required in connection with the control of advertising and sponsorship by the BHA; • any VAT payable in respect of these sums.

Appearance Money

4Where a racecourse decides to add their own Appearance Money payments into either the conditions of the race or the Total Race Value , these amounts must be clearly advertised in the race conditions and paid to connections in accordance with paragraph 3.

Races With More Prizes Than Declared Runners

5If, after the deadline for Declarations to Run and before the Race is declared ‘Off’, a race has fewer declared runners than the number of placings to which money or prizes are due to be allocated, the surplus shall be deducted from the amount due from the Racecourse in relation to the Total Prize Fund for the Race.

Races Not Run Following the Making of a Division

6After the payment of Prize Money and any refunds in relation to horses allocated to a division that was subsequently abandoned, any Stake money remaining shall be paid to the credit of the Race Division Fund.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Stewards Assistant Stewards Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: ENTRY FEES AND PRIZE MONEY (previously in Rules of Racing)
entries.html:
ENTRY FEES

1All fees payable in respect of entering into and running in a race must be in accordance with the scales laid down from time to time by the BHA.

2The conditions of the race must state the fees relating to any race stage and the total liability for runners.

PRIZE MONEY

3The minimum Total Prize Fund in a race must not be less than that laid down from time to time by the BHA.

4No prize, outside of that payable under the Rules, may be offered to any p erson other than trainer, rider, stable staff or breeder with out the prior approval of the BHA. Such prizes must be included in the conditions of the race and must not be included in the calculation of prize money for the race payable under the Rules.

5Unless it is a prize already approved by the BHA under paragraph 4, t he value of any non-monetary prize must be advertised.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Stewards Assistant Stewards Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: PARADES (previously in Rules of Racing)
entries.html:
1A parade is mandatory and must be advertised in the conditions of the race in:

• each Group 1 flat race (subject to paragraph 2), and • each Grade 1 jump race which is not a Grade 1 novice or Juvenile jump race.

but, where there are two or more such races on a racecard, a parade is mandatory in the principal race only.

2There shall be no p arades in races confined to two years old or any flat race less than seven furlongs.

3A parade is optional in all other races but, where a Racecourse Managing Executive wishes to e xercise the option of having a p arade, permission must be sought from the Authority's Jump Racing or Flat Racing Committee respectively.

4The Racecourse Managing Executive is responsible for deciding upon the order in which the parade is to take place e.g. race card or non-race card order/10 second release/led to the half furlong marker/to beyond the winning post etc..

5In order to ensure all persons involved in the parade are aware of the order:

• The conditions of the parade order must be specified in the race card; • Notices detailing the conditions must be p ublished on the notice board in the weighing room. • The Stewards must be advised of the conditions at the Raceday Team Briefing and confirmation provided of the person responsible for organising the runners; NOTE: Where, in exceptional circumstances, changes have to be made to the published details of parades, the Stewards must be notified.

6Permission for any privileges in the parade e.g. early to post, must be requested through the Stewards.

7A parade may be assisted by one or more outriders at the front or rear.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Stewards Assistant Stewards Inspectors of Courses Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: RACING CALENDAR AND PROGRAMME BOOK PROOFS (previously BHAGI 2.1)
entries.html:
Racing Calendar Proofs

1The Racing Calendar Proofs are to completed on the NRAS software to the deadlines laid out in Proofing Schedule section of Race Management.

Programme Book Proofs

2These proofs are made available to the nominated representative of the Managing Executive approximately 5 months before the commencement of the period covered by the Programme Book in question for all meetings which are to be in cluded in that Book. The proofs must be returned to the Racing Department with such amendments as are required by the date stipulated.

General

3All proofs will be made electronically via the NRAS software and must be returned to the Racing Department in the same manner.

4The Managing Executive is responsible for ensuring that accurate copy of race programmes and all related information including Safety Factors (as issue d by the Racecourse Department) is received by the Racing Department.

5Failure to return proofs, as stipulated above, either for the Racing Calendar or for Programme Books, is a breach of this Instruction. In this event the BHA will make such decisions about the content of programmes or race conditions as they consi der appropriate without r eference to the relevant Managing Executive in order to ensure timely publication.

6A change made at the request of a racecourse to race conditions, after the original publication of the programme, will result in a charge unless the circumstances are shown to be outside the control of that racecourse.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: STAKES/CLOSING DATES/SUPPLEMENTARY ENTRIES (previously BHAGI 2.2)
entries.html:
Stakes - Flat Races

1The stakes for all Flat races, other than Pattern races, are to be not more than 0.5% of the Total Prize Fund.

2The stakes for all Pattern races are to be not more than:

Group 1 – 1% of the Total Prize Fund; Group 2 – 0.85% of the Total Prize Fund; Group 3 – 0.7% of the Total Prize Fund.

Except for racecourses which have signed a Premier Prize Money Agreement, in which case the stakes for all Pattern races are not to be more than:

Group 1 – 1.25% of the Total Prize Fund; Group 2 – 1.00% of the Total Prize Fund; Group 3 – 1.00% of the Total Prize Fund.

3Except by special permission of the BHA, the stakes in Early Closing races will be split:

a)Races closing between 9 weeks and 10 months before running:

If two scratching deadline stages, no more than 25% at entry, the combined entry and payment if not scratched by the first scratching deadline must not exceed 50%, balance spread between the payment if not scratched by the second scratching deadline and confirmation stages;

If one scratching deadline stage, no more than 25% at entry, balance spread between the payment if not scratched by the scratching deadline and confirmation stages;

b)Races closing between 4 weeks and 8 weeks 6 days before running:

No more than 35% at entry, balance spread between scratching deadline and confirmation stages;

c)Races closing between 16 and 22 days before running:

30% at entry, balance at confirmation stage.

Stakes - Steeple Chases, Hurdle Races and National Hunt Flat Races

4The stakes for all Steeple Chases and Hurdle races and N ational Hunt Flat races are to be not more than 0.5% of the Total Prize Fund.

5Except by special permission of the BHA, the stakes in Early Closing races will be split:

a)Races closing 4 or more weeks before running:

Not more than 25% at entry, balance spread between scratching deadline and confirmation stages;

b)Races closing between 16 and 22 days before running:

30% at entry, balance at confirmation stage.

Closing Dates

6Except by special permission of the BHA, the following restrictions will apply to the closing dates of races:

Flat Races

a)Group 1 races to close no more than 9 weeks before running , with the exception of the Derby;

b)Group 2 races to close no more than 7 weeks before running;

c)Heritage Handicaps to close no more than 6 weeks before running;

d)With the exception of any other race with a Total Prize Fund of £100,000 or more, all other races will close 5 or 6 days before running;

e)Group 1 and Group 2 races confined to 2 year olds to close no more than 7 weeks before running.

Jump Races

f)With the exception of Pattern r aces or any other ra ce with a Total Prize Fund of £50,000 or more, all races will close 5 or 6 days before running.

Supplementary Entries

7.

Flat Races

a)Group 1 races that close more than 12 weeks before running must provide for supplementary entries in the race conditions.

b)Any other early closing Group 1 or Group 2 race may provide for supplementary entries in the race conditions at the option of the Managing Executive.

The cost of the supplementary entry shall not exceed 10% of the Total Prize Fund but shall be sufficient such as to make this route relatively unattractive (i.e. ideally more than 5%).

Jump Races

c)Any early cl osing Grade 1 Jump Pattern race may provide for supplementary entries in the race conditions at the option of the Managing Executive.

d)Any other non -early closing Grade 1 or Grade 2 race may provide for supplementary entries in the race conditions at the option of the Managing Executive. Such supplementary en tries will close at 12 noon, 72 hours prior to the race.

The cost of the supplementary entry shall not exceed 5% of the Total Prize Fund but shall be sufficient such as to make this route relatively unattractive. In the case of rescheduled races which c ontain provision for a supplementary entry, the supplementary entry may be reduced down to 2.5% of the Total Prize Fund.

Note: A portion of the supplementary entry payment which is equal to the full stake payable through the early entry system shall be in cluded within the Total Prize Fund. The latest full stake will be used where more than one entry stage is advertised. The remainder of the supplementary payment will not form part of the total Prize Money the racecourse guarantees to be available for dist ribution in a Total Prize Fund race, but shall be added to the total Prize Money.

Normal Closers

8Handicap races closing 5 or 6 days before running may include a split entry fee at the option of the Managing Executive.

a)Horses rated within the adver tised rating range in Flat races will be required to pay 100% of the advertised stake. Horses rated below the advertised rating range of the race will be permitted to enter and will pay 20% of the advertised stake at entry and the remaining 80% stake if declaring to run.

b)Horses rated within 26lb of the advertised upper rating band of the race in Jump races will be required to pay 100% of the advertised stake. Horses rated 27lb or more below the advertised upper rating band of the race will be permitte d to enter and will pay 20% of the advertised stake at entry and the remaining 80% stake if declaring to run.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: ADVERTISED VALUES (previously BHAGI 2.3)
entries.html:
Criteria Fixtures

1All races run at Criteria fixtures shall have advertised values within the appropriate minimum and maximum values where applicable.

Total Prize Funds

2Except with the permission of the BHA, races must be adv ertised as Total Prize Fund races.

Non-Criteria Fixtures

3All races classifie d in Classes 1 and 2 run at Non -Criteria fixtures shall have advertised values within the appropriate minimum and maximum values , as determined by the BHA for races run at Criteria fi xtures. All races run at these fixtures in Classes 3 and below shall not be governed by any such arrangements but shall have their advertised values approved by the BHA.

Note: Criteria, and Non -Criteria fixtures are fixtures , which have been so designat ed within the criteria promulgated by the Horserace Betting Levy Board.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: RACE PROGRAMMING (previously BHAGI 2.4)
entries.html:
Flat Pattern Races

1Any changes to Flat Pattern races, or proposals to upgrade a Listed race to within the Pattern, must be agreed by the Flat Pattern Committee and subsequently approved by the BHA Board and, where appropriate, the European Pattern Committee.

Jump Pattern Races

2Any changes to races within the Jump Pattern must be agreed by the Jump Pattern Committee and subsequently approved by the BHA Board.

Apprentice Races

3Except with the permission of the Racing Department, all Racecourses staging Flat races shall have at least one race confined to Apprentice Jockeys for every 4 days’ Flat racing.

4In Apprentice races, it is reco mmended to include an all owance(s) for less experienced jockeys.

Conditional Jockeys

5Except with the permission of the Racing Department, all Racecourses staging Jump racing shall have at least one Hurdle race or Steeple Chase confined to Conditional Jockeys for every 3 days’ Jump racing, excluding Mixed days.

6Such race(s) may NOT be a Steeple Chase confined to Maidens or Novices. No restriction is to be placed on the number of winners which jockeys may have ridden but it is recommended to include allowances for less experienced jockeys.

Brush Hurdle Races

7Whenever a racecourse wishes to programme a race involving the use of the Brush Hurdle prior approval to do so must be obtained from the Racing Group.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Handicappers Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: RACE TITLES (previously BHAGI 2.6)
entries.html:
Race Titles

1The following information shall be incorporated into the title of every race or stated after the title as an adjunct to it:

(i)Type of race (Excluding Pattern races referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 below);*

(ii)Group or Grade category (for Flat or Jump Pattern races only);

(iii)Fact of Listed status;

(iv)Fact of restriction of jockeys to Apprentices, Conditional Jockeys or Amateur Jockeys;*

(v)Fact of restriction to fillies and mares only;*

(vi)Race Classification.

Note 1: Standard Handicaps and Open Maidens should be described simply as Handicaps or Maidens in their titles.

Note 2: * Indicates information which may be incorporated in brackets after the main body of the title.

2The titles of all Pattern and Listed races are to include a permanent word to establish the continuity of the race (the ‘race handle’). A sponsor’s name may be added as a prefix or a suffix to, but is not to replace the established race handle. In the case of Flat Group 3 and Listed races and all Jump Grade 2 and Listed races, the race handle may appear in brackets after the title, preceded by ‘Registered as ….’

3In the case of any newly created Flat Group 2s a race handle may be referred to as ‘Registered as’ until that particular sponsorship deal is terminated, at which time the race handle must be incorporated within the main title. In the case of existing races which are upgraded to Flat Group 2 status, the race handle may remain as ‘Registered as’ at the specific request of the existing sponsor, until that particular sponsorship deal is terminated, at which stage the permanent race handle must be incorporated within the main title.

4The titles of existing sponsored Flat and Jump Pattern and Listed races which have no established name may remain unaltered until the sponsorship is renewed or terminated. At this point a race handle is to be added.

5If a race is named after King Edward VII, a member of their family or any descendent of them by birth or marriage who bears or bore a Royal title, the name of any sponsor of the race shall appear after the name or title of the royal personage in question.

6The title of any race must be deemed by the Racing Department to be appropriate and sensible in its content and structure. Race titles potentially deemed to be carrying a political message will be considered inappropriate.

7Race titles must be limited to a maximum of 50 characters (including spaces) , excluding race type and conditions-related words such as ‘two-years-old’, ‘E.B.F.’ and Race handles, unless approval has been granted in exceptional circumstances by the Racing Department to waive this requirement.

8In the case of Race handles in non -Pattern and Listed races, racecourses may apply to register a handle with the Racing Department. Once registered this handle may not be changed within five years, unless approval has been granted in exceptional circumstances by the Racing Department to waive this requirement.

9Race titles advertising website addresses must not include standard URL prefixes such as ‘http://’ or ‘www’.

10The repetition of a race title where the race types are identical must be avoided.

11Race titles containing premium-rate telephone numbers or SMS numbers will not be permitted.

12Managing Executives should also be mindful of the overuse of text pages and telephone numbers in race titles in view of the problems they create for both commentators and the media, and the likelihood that, in consequence, the race title could be abbreviated or omitted altogether.

Holborn Gate Circulation 26 Southampton Buildings Racecourse Association London WC2A 1AN

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: INSTRUCTIONS RELATING TO SPECIAL RACES (previously BHAGI 2.7)
entries.html:
General

1The parameters relating to the acceptability and operation of certain ‘special’ races are set out below.

Races Restricted to Horses Sold at Specific Auctions

2The conditions and date of the race must be acceptable to the Racing Department.

3The added money must come from the Racecourse or sponsorship funds rather than being financed from a sales pool levied upon either the vendors or purchasers at the sales.

4The race must be staged as an additional race and must not replace an existing opportunity for the horse population.

5Subject to the discretion of the Racing Group, only one such race restricted to a specific auction may be staged in any particular year.

Handicap Hunters’ Steeple Chases

6Permission to stage a Handicap Hunters’ Steeple Chase must be sought from the Racing Group prior to programming.

7The race must be run as an Open handicap, without any rating restriction and must meet the minimum prize money meritocracy level for a Class 3 Steeple Chase.

8The race must be restricted to horses which have run in three Hunters’ Steeple Chases since the start of the previous calendar year and which have not won a Class 1 or 2 Steeple Chase since the start of the previous calendar year.

9The race must be staged as an additional race and must not replace an existing opportunity for the horse population.

Series and Series Sponsorship

10Application must be made to the Racing Department of any projected Series at the earliest planning stage so that it may be considered by the Racing Group.

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: Instruction BHAGI 2.11
entries.html:
11All new Race Series Finals must be programmed at a minimum of Class 2 and have a minimum total prize fund of £30,000 (or £40,000 for all Race Series Finals from 1 April 2026 onwards) in order to be considered.

Holborn Gate Circulation 26 Southampton Buildings Handicappers London WC2A 1AN Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: INSTRUCTIONS AND GUIDELINES FOR RACE TIMES AND ORDER OF RUNNING (previously BHAGI 2.8)
entries.html:
Race Times

1At all meetings other than floodlit meetings, the last race is to be timed to start not later than 10 minutes before sunset.

2Normally, there is to be an advertised interval of 30 (the minimum) or 35 minutes between races. The nominated representative of the Managing Executive must apply to the Racing Department for this to be reduced to 25 minutes in special circumstances, but this shorter interval will normally only be agreed for one of the first two intervals of an evening Flat meeting.

3When an afternoon/evening has three meetings they should be programmed to have 10 minute intervals between their respective advertised race times.

In exceptional circumstances, and after discussion with the Managing Executive concerned, the Racing Department will set appropriate advertised race times in order to prevent a serious clash of 5 minutes or less between two or more meetings, doing everything possible to avoid moving the first race time earlier.

Alteration of Advertised Race Times

4When a race or race meeting is abandoned or otherwise impacted by external events, at short notice it may be desirable for the advertised race times at that race meeting, or another meeting(s) taking place on the same day to be altered to produce the best possible pattern of racing and restore regular intervals between races and /or account for the change in circumstances.

In such scenarios one of two approaches may be followed:

5a) Where the matter has arisen before 10:30 on the day before Racing, the Racing Department will contact the nominated representative of the Managing Executive concerned and may request that the advertised race times are altered.

Updates will be made so that such altered race times become the new official advertised times and will appear in all publications from that point.

Such an alteration could change the race time to earlier or later than originally advertised.

5b) Where the matter has arisen after 10:30 on the day before Racing, s ubject to the agreement of the Managing Executive and, the Stewards of the Meeting, the Stewards of the Meeting, the Racing Department will request a delay to the published race time, which will remain unaltered. Races will not be requested to be run earlier than BHAGI 2.12 Dtd 28 March 2026

advertised race time under this approach.

6In both scenarios, the Racing Department will duly notify the media (if time permits), SIS, TRP, Betting Operators, Data and Integrity Service Providers and the Racing Calendar Office.

The nominated representative of the Managing Executive must, in turn, ensure that all relevant personnel at the racecourse are notified of the revised race times together with ensuring that appropriate public announcements are made. In particular, they must ensure that the Stewards are fully informed

7These procedures will only operate when it is determined that the change in circumstances since the publication of declarations merits either an alteration or a delay to the advertised race times in the view of the BHA Special Considerations Regarding Order of Running

8Races restricted to two years old should be placed as early as possible in the order of running and no weight-for-age race restricted to Novices or Maidens of any age should be placed last on a programme.

9Selling or Claiming races are not to be placed as the last race on the programme.

10Wherever possible, the following should be complied with:

a)the respective distance of races and the position of the start to be taken into account in compiling a meeting's order of running to assist in ensuring that races start on time; b) Apprentice, Conditional or Amateur races (Hunters’ Chases excepted, see part c)) to be placed first on any programme in order that they may vacate the weighing room in a timely manner; c) Hunters’ Steeple Chases to be placed as the last Steeple Chase on a programme

.

Holborn Gate 26 Southampton Buildings Circulation London WC2A 1AN Stewards Assistant Stewards Clerks of the Scales Judges Starters Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: RACE ABANDONMENT AT FIVE DAY ENTRY STAGE/ RE-OPENED RACES AT ENTRY (previously BHAGI 2.9)
entries.html:
Race Abandonment – Scope

1Any race which is not a Pattern, Listed, Early Closing race or the final of a ra ce Series and which rec eives fewer than 5 entries may be abandoned by the Managing Executive. (Note: An entry for a horse which is not qualified at the time of entry shall not count). Before a race is abandoned the Managing Executive must contact the Tr ainers of the entered h orses to ascertain their intentions to run. The Managing Executive will then, in conjunction with the Racing Department, decide whether the race is to be abandoned.

2The BHA has instructed that only one race on any card may be aband oned in this way, but will waive this restriction in exceptional circumstances.

Race Abandonment - Procedure

3In the event that the Managing Executive does wish to abandon a race, the nominated representative of the Managing Executive must notify the Racing Department, Tel (0207 152 0050) as soon as possible , and no later than 11:00am on the day after the race in question has closed.

Note: Should a race be abandoned, the Weatherbys Racing Operations Department will inform all Trainers who hold an entry for that race of the decision.

4When a race is abandoned after having received fewer than 5 entries, it must be replaced by dividing the weight-for-age race on the same card with the highest number of entries. The divided race may not be a Pattern, Listed, or an Early Closing race. In exceptional circumstances a race other than a weight -for-age race may be divided but only with the express permission of the Racing Department. If the race to be divided is more valuable than the race which has been abandoned, the Managing Executive must provide the additional prize money to run the division of this race at its advertised value.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: DIVISION OF RACES, ELIMINATION OF RUNNERS, REVISIONS TO ORDER OF RUNNING AFTER DECLARATION (previously BHAGI 2.10)
entries.html:
Division of Races or Elimination of Runners

1Unless advised otherwise the Racing Calendar Office will di vide or eliminate to the Safety Factor and the Field Size Limits published in the race conditions in the Racing Calendar.

Provisional Times

2The Clerk of the Course or their nominated representative must ascertain the number of entries for each race on the days on which entries (other than for early closing races) close either by reference to racingadmin.co.uk, or by telephoning the Weatherbys Racing Operations Department (01933 440011) between 2:30pm and 4:30 pm. When it appears likely that the division of a race under Rule (I)9 will be necessary the Clerk of the Course or their nominated representative must give provisional times for the additional divisions to the Weatherbys Racing Operations Department (01933 440011) as soon as possible but no later than the time fixed for declarations under the Race Entry Code (REC), para 33. Failure to do this will cause the Racing Department to set the advertised race time(s) for the additional division(s).

3At all fixtures w here a race division t akes place, this will ge nerally lead to a later race being scheduled, unless prohibited from doing so by sunset times . Should racecourses wish to seek an earlier start, they must contact the Racing Department, and should the date of declaration fall on a weekend or Bank Holiday, prior approval should be sought.

4In exceptional circumstances, and after discussion with the Managing Executive concerned, the Racing Department will set an appropriate time for the extra division(s) in order to prevent an unacceptable gap or clash with race times at other meetings.

Changes to Order of Running after Declaration to Run

5The BHA will not normally authorise a change to the order of running of races after the time fixed for declaration to run un der the REC, para 33 unless the procedures outlined below have been invoked. If exceptional circumstances prevail, application may be made to the BHA Racing Operations Manager for the order of running of races to be altered. This request should be made as soon as possible but no later than 1 hour after the time for declaration to run. If the request relates to racing on a Monday, the request should be directed to the Weatherbys Racing Operations Department (01933 440011). It should also be understood that if the request is approved, and it therefore necessitates the Weatherbys Racing Operations Department advising a number of Trainers that their race is being run earlier or later than the advertised time, a fee to cover the cost of telephoning the Trainers will be charged. The latter provision does not apply when a race is divided. BHAGI 2.14 Dtd 1 April 2023

6Where seven or fewer horses are declared to run, the time for declarations shall be extended as referred to in the REC, para 37 but the race in question will retain its position in the order of running provided more than one horse is declared to run. If only one horse is declared to run the race will be placed last on the programme. If a race receives no declarations to run, despite the application of the time extension, the race will be declared void

Walk Overs

7A Walk-Over may take place at a practicable time either before the first race or after the last race e.g. 15 minutes. However, where a Walk -Over occurs due to non - runners on race-day the Walk-Over must still take place at the advertised time.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Stewards Assistant Stewards Clerks of the Scales Judges Starters Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: SPONSORSHIP OF RACES (previously BHAGI 2.11)
entries.html:
Sponsorship Details

1Managing Executives are required to complete the annual prize money analysis issued by the Racing Calendar Office. This print o ut requires the Managing Executive to confirm race sponsorship figures from the previous year.

Penalty Value

2By the date fixed for entry or, in early closing races, confirmation of entries , it must be possible to ascertain from the conditions the full va lue of the race to the win ner. However, in cases where a race is transferred to another racecourse due to abandonment the full value of the race may be subject to alteration. Except by permission of the BHA, the winning owner is not to receive from the sp onsor, either directly or indirectly, any monies save those permitted by Stakes and Prize Money Code or under any controls for sponsorship approved by the BHA.

Series Sponsorship

3Application must be made to the Racing Department of any projected series at the earliest planning stage so that it may be considered by the Racing Group Race Series – moved to BHAGI 2.11 paras 10 & 11

Sponsored Attendants’ Clothing

4Whenever attendants’ clothing is going to be provided by the race sponsors it should be include d in or added to the race conditions . If unable to add to the race conditions because it is past the ‘post published changes’ time, trainers with runners at the meeting/race (as applicable) must be advised directly.

5The only two meetings where the accept ance of attendants’ clothing is compulsory are the Aintree Grand National Festival and the Epsom Derby Festival. At all other meetings where attendants’ clothing is provided racecourses must ensure that staff are fully aware that accepting and wearing the clothing is not mandatory and that they should not accept any clothing unless they are c arrying another form of sponsorship relating to their owner/yard.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: CUPS OR TROPHIES (previously BHAGI 2.12)
entries.html:
Races with a Total Prize Fund of £25,000 or more

1Any cup or trophy offered in such races may either be classed as:

(i)optional and included in the prize money;

(ii)treated as an additional trophy and excluded from prize money.

Unless the BHA gives permission for a higher value, any cup or trophy shall not exceed £2,000 or 5% of the Total Prize Fund, whichever is the lesser amount. Where permission is given, the BHA must be pr ovided with proof of purchase in order to ascertain the exact value of the trophy.

Sponsored Races and those with a Total Prize Fund of £6,000 or more

2If a cup or trophy is to be awarded in these races it will either be classed as optional or additional.

3Optional cups or trophies will be valued at no more than 5% of the Total Prize Fund of the race in question and their acceptance will be dependant upon completion of the form detailed in Annex A.

Note: For the purposes of this Instruction a race is not deemed to be sponsored unless a minimum of £500 is added by the sponsor.

Unsponsored Races with a Total Prize Fund of up to £5,999

4Except with permission of the BHA, such races will only offer cups or trophies classed as mementoes on the basis laid down in paragraph 5, below. The award of the memento will also be included in the race conditions.

Mementoes

5Additional cups or trophies must be described as mementoes in the conditions of the race. They will be:

a)of no stated value;

b)not included in the prize money.

Note: The form set out in Annex B is not applicable to such mementoes.

6Managing Executives may alternatively offer owners of winners in any race with no cup or trophy the opportunity to purchase a memento for n ot more than 5% of the Total Prize Fund. These will have to be paid for by owners immediately on the day unless the Managing Executive either wishes to use the form detailed in Annex B or invoices the owners.

Challenge Cups

7Challenge Cups not permanentl y retained by the owner are outside the scope of this Instruction.

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: FIELD SIZE LIMITS (previously BHAGI 2.13)
entries.html:
Adjustment of Field Size Limit

1If a Managing Executive wishes to adjust the Field Size Limit for any race(s) application to do so must be made to t he Racing Department in wr iting, citing the reasons, no later than one month prior to the publication of the race(s) conditions in the Racing Calendar.

Race Exemptions from Field Size Limits

2A Managing Executive may apply to the Racing Department f or any race with a Total Prize Fund in excess of £30,000 to be exempt from the imposition of a Field Size Limit, subject to compliance with the Safety Factor for the race. Such application must be made in writing no later than one month prior to the public ation of the race conditio ns in the Racing Calendar.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: RESERVES (previously BHAGI 2.14)
entries.html:
Races Eligible for the Inclusion of Reserves

1A Managing Executive may apply to the Racing Department for the inclusion of reserves in those races which are classified as follows:

(i)Group 1 Flat races;

(ii)Heritage Handicaps;

(iii)Grade 3 Jump Handicaps with 48-hour declarations.

2An application for the inclusion of reserves in any other race, or any deviation from the conditions as set out below, must be made to the Racing Department at the earliest planning stage so that it may be considered by the Racing Group in advance of publication of the race conditions.

Determination of Reserves

3The race conditions must stipulate the maximum number of runners and the maximum number of reserves.

4The trainers of horses which may be eliminated from the race must indicate at the declaration stage whether they are prepared for their horse to be a reserve. If a trainer does not make any such indication and cannot be contacted immediately after the declaration stage, the horse will not stand as a reserve.

5In the event that the number of declared horses exceeds the maximum number of runners, reserves will be selected from amongst those which are subject to elimination and have confirmed to the Racing Calendar Office that they are prepared to stand as a reserve, in order of their position in the elimination sequence (in handicaps, as most recently adjusted to take account of penalties). Where two or more horses have identical ratings or assessments in a weight -for-age race or identical weights in a handicap race, their position in the elimination sequence will have been allocated by random ballot.

6The reserves will be placed in order in accordance with the elimination sequence, with the first reserve being the reserve with the highest elimination sequence number. Each reserve will be given its own racecard number. For the avoidance of any doubt, in a race with a safety factor of 30 and three reserves, the first reserve would b e allotted a racecard number of 31, the second reserve 32 and the third reserve 33.

7When making the draw for Flat races, a reserve will be allotted a draw position. This position would be removed from the Starting Stalls in the event that the reserve does not run. For the avoidance of any doubt, in a race with a safety factor of 30 BHAGI 2.18 Dtd 1 October 2019

and three reserves, the declared horses including the reserves would be allotted a draw between 1 and 33.

Replacement of a Declared Runner with a Reserve

8In the event of a n on-runner being notified t o the Racing Calendar Office by 1:00pm on the day before the race, the first reserve will replace that non-runner.

9If there are further non -runners by this time, the remaining reserves will replace those horses in the same way.

10Declarations of riders f or any reserves which obtain a ru n will be required by 1:30pm the day before the race.

11In handicap races in which a reserve has been afforded the opportunity to run, weights will be raised at 1:00pm on the day before the race in the same manner as at the 48-hour declaration stage if there are any relevant non -runners notified to the Racing Calendar Office by that time. Should the weights be raised at this time, revised declaration of riders will be accepted for all declared runners up to 1:30pm on the same day.

12All payments made prior to the race for any horse which is eliminated or is a reserve and was subsequently not afforded the opportunity to run shall be returned.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 2 - Race Planning
entries.title: The Draw - Special Conditions
entries.html:
Special Conditions Relating to Non-Standard Draws in Flat Races

1A racecourse may apply to the Racing Department for dispensation to conduct a manual draw for a Class 2 Flat race, in place of the standard automated draw. Any such application must be submitted in writing in advance of the race appearing in the Racing dispensation is granted, the draw to be conducted as follows:

1Draw to be held as soon as possible after Declarations close at 10am

2Draw to be filmed and televised live

3Horses to be drawn one at a time, followed by either:

a)A further draw indicating the stall number

b)The stall to be selected by the Owner, Trainer or their representative, one of which must be present. (Separate protocols exist for this type of draw and are available from the Racing Department if required).

4Numbers and horses to be printed on balls (or similar), to be placed inside casings or any such object as can be fairly and randomly mixed without numbers being outwardly visible.

5The drum or bowl to hold the horses and stall numbers to be regularly and thoroughly turned or mixed throughout the draw.

6Equipment to be put in place at least one week prior to the draw and signed off as suitable by the Racing Department.

7A member of the Racing Department (or representative) be present to adjudicate over the draw, with the authority to make any alterations as necessary or order a re-draw on the day, if he/she has any concerns over the validity of the draw.

75 High Holborn Circulation London WC1V 6LS Racecourse Association

entries.doc: SECTION 3 - The Racecourse
entries.title: Notification Of Equine Events/Racing Surface Restrictions/Racecourse Gallops Racecourse Access By Other Ungulate (Hooved) Animals
entries.html:
Notification of Equine Events

1Notification of any event which ( exclusive of meetings run under the Rules of Racing or para 5, 6 and 10) must be made to the Racecourse Operations Department at Head Office at least 10 business days before that event is due to take place. The following details must be given:

a)name of the promoting organisation;

b)where on the racecourse property the event is to be held;

c)whether or not the official racecourse stables will be used;

d)how long the horses/ponies will remain on the property;

e)the steps which the Managing Executive and that organisation intend to take to comply with the requirements of the Vaccinations Code and BHAGI 7.2.

Racing Surface Restrictions

2Where any part of the racing surface is to be used the above notification must also include an application for authorisation, giving full details of the use to which the track will be put.

3O nly in very exceptional circumstances will authorisation be given if the event is to take place less than ten days before the next fixture run under the Rules of Racing on the same turf track.

4Aircraft are NOT to be allowed to land on the racing surface. During a meeting NO aircraft must be allowed to land or take off from the racecourse without the express permission of a nominated representative of the Managing Executive.

Racecourse Gallops – racing surface

5For turf racecourses, gallops taking place on the racing surface on race days are not permitted unless

a)prior permission has been granted by the Racecourse Operations Department, and

b)the gallop takes place after racing has ended.

6For all-weather racecourses, gallops may take place on the racing surface on a race day provided that they are completed and all horses have left the track with sufficient time for standard preparation of the surface to be carried out in advance of racing.

7A racecourse gallop must not take place whilst a Stalls Test or Pre -Race Assessment is in progress. Veterinary and Medical arrangements are at the discretion of the Managing Executive subject to compliance with any relevant legislation or government guidance.

8Racecourses should maintain auditable records of the number of horses galloping and the yard from which they have come from, for review when requested.

Racecourse Gallops – announcements

9W henever a racecourse gallop is scheduled to take place on a race day announcements should be made on the racecourse to advise the public of:

a)the name of the horse(s)

b)the name of the rider(s)

c)t he distance of the gallop

d)the time of the gallop

Racecourse Gallops on Non-Race Day

10Racecourse gallops on non- race days are not allowed unless permission has been obtained from the Racecou rse Operations Department in accordance with the following procedures:

a)Applications on the required form https://www.cognitoforms.com/BritishHorseracingAuthority/RacecourseOpe rationsRequestForm m ust be submitted by 1 December each year and must include a risk assessment for Veterinary and Medical cover that will be in place.

b)Accurate records must be maintained and supplied quarterly to the BHA (and on request in the event of any equine health outbreak ) on the applicable form detailing

• Date of gallopers • Number of horses • Training yards

c)Veterinary and Medical arrangements are the responsibility of the Managing Executive.

Racecourse access by other ungulate (hooved) animals

11No ungulate animal (commonly known examples of ungulates are horses, zebras, donkeys, cattle, bison, camelids, goats, pigs, sheep and many species kept in zoos) may enter racecourse premises without the explicit permission of the Racecourse Operations Department other than: a) Horses and ponies engaged to run at the meeting; b) Gallopers as per para 5 - 10 above. c) Horses and companion horses/ponies travelling between race meetings per BHAGI 7.2 Para 9. 12. Any racecourse hosting such an event must ensure they obtain a pre-event health declaration showing that the animals are healthy, free from disease and there are no contagious, infectious, or zoonotic diseases on the premises where the animals usually reside. 13. The principal areas where the animals were housed on the day must be properly disinfected after use. 14. All horses, donkeys and ponies attending the e vent must be vaccinated in accordance with the Vaccination Code. Checks of their respective passports and vaccination records must be carried out prior to the event. 15. Records of • pre-event health declarations • proper disinfection and • vaccination checks

must be maintained and made available to the Racing Operations Department upon request.

75 High Holborn London WC1V 6LS Circulation Inspectors of Courses Veterinary Officers Racecourse Association Stewards Assistant Stewards

entries.doc: SECTION 3 - The Racecourse
entries.title: The Condition Of The Course, Going & Irrigation
entries.html:
Introduction

1This BHAGI has been written in two parts. The first part covers the mandatory requirements. Annexes A and B have been developed in conjunction with the Racecourse Association and are provided for best practice guidance.

Racing Surface

2The Managing Executive is responsible for the condition of the course as stated in BHAGI 1.4 and must aim to produce consistent ground and to maintain this consistency during a race meeting, in line with industry best practice.

Clearly, there will be times when racecourses are unable to influence their ground owing to weather conditions (e.g. after heavy rainfall) but Jump courses should aim to provide Good ground (and no firmer than Good to Firm) . Flat courses should aim to provide Good to Firm ground. It is accepted that some Managing Executives of Flat and Jump courses may wish to produce Good and Good to Soft ground, respectively, depending upon their track topography, soil type, weather and fixture patterns and/or whether they are staging two or more consecutive days racing. To optimise recovery of the sward, the ground must be ‘put back’ as soon as possible after any use of the racing surface. (See also Annex A paragraph 8). Sufficient raceday staff should be employed to tread in the course (particularly bends) between races. At Jump meetings Fence Attendants may carry out this duty.

Managing Executives must inform the Raceday Stewards of all works involving the displacement of the racing surface which have been carried out since the previous meeting.

All-Weather Racecourses – Maintenance and Records

3In the case of a synthetic ( All Weather ) Track, the racing surface is to be maintained in accordance with the surface manufacturers’ recommendations and/or as agreed with the Racecourse Operations Department. Furthermore, records of the refurbishment work and any other non -routine maintenance work which is carried out must also be kept and made available for inspection by the Inspector of Courses. The course must also be reinstated as necessary during racing in order to maintain consistent going.

For the benefit of the racecourse as a management tool, accurate records of the following must be kept, the frequency depending on the course’s fixture programme: (i) rainfall for a 48 hour period prior to every fixture (representing the amount which has fallen on the racing surface); (ii) maximum and minimum air temperatures; BHAGI 3.2 Dtd 28 March 2026

(iii)surface and subsurface ground temperatures; (iv) irrigation applied in inches or millimetres over given periods and areas; (v) moisture content of artificial surface

Turf Racecourses - Records

4For the benefit of the racecourse as a management tool , accurate records of the following must be kept, the frequency depending on the course’s fixture programme:

(i)rainfall (representing the amount which has fallen on the racing surface);

(ii)maximum and minimum air temperatures;

(iii)surface and subsurface ground temperatures (using a ground minimum thermometer and 100mm sub surface soil thermometer); (iv) irrigation applied in inches or millimetres over given periods and areas;

(v)routine maintenance (i.e. method of putting ground back, fertiliser application, wetting agents, mowing, aeration treatments, compaction relief, top dressing rates and material etc);

(vi)movement of running rail;

(vii)any instances of consistent standing water.

Management

5Managing Executives must retain the services of a turf consultant (and/or synthetic (All Weather) consultant as applicable) . The Managing Executive is to produce by the end of October each year the turf consultant’s report on the condition of the course (which can be an individual report or a series of reports if multiple visits are undertaken. A copy must be sent to the Racecourse Operations Department. The timing of turf consultants’ visits should be varied from year to year so that the course can be assessed at different times of the course’s racing calendar. The following detail should be included:

(i)Surface makeup of the racetrack, to include desirable grasses, undesirable grasses, weeds, moss, algae, pests and diseases.

(ii)Surface and profile consolidation levels

(iii)Root depth and density

(iv)A soil analysis with the following items listed:

a)pH b) Phosphate c) Potassium d) Magnesium e) Organic matter BHAGI 3.2 Dtd 28 March 2026

f)Sand g) Silt h) Clay

(v)Infiltration rates and any drainage problems; Irrigation water must be tested for PH, salinity.

(vi)Fertilising regime

(vii)Irrigation regime and efficiency

(viii)Track repair regime

(ix)Equipment/machinery needs

6In the case of a synthetic (All Weather) Track, the Managing Executive concerned must produce to the Racecourse Operations Department by the end of October an annual report compiled by an independent consultant on the condition of the racing surface. This will include at representative intervals the distances from the inside running rail on a track prepared for racing:

(i)the depth of the cushion and pad

(ii)infiltration rates through the pad and base of the track

(iii)an overall material composition percentage breakdown

(iv)a binder effectiveness assessment if applicable

(v)a grading of sand particle size

(vi)consolidation levels of the surface

Note: Racecourses may wish to include other tests for analytical purposes (e.g biometrical or microscopic assessments) in addition to the above mandatory requirements.

Fixture Allocation

7Fixture allocation in relation to racecourse 'going' will be reviewed annually by the Racecourse Operations Department (including the Inspectors of Courses) in conjunction with the Racing Department on the basis of 5 years’ going and abandonment data to allow for sig nificant climatic fluctuations. Managing Executives must therefore consult the BHA’s Optimum Use of the Turf documentation (compiled annually for each course) to ensure their pattern of fixtures is appropriate and conducive to good turf management.

Where a course consistently fails to meet the going aims laid down in paragraph 2, the Racecourse Operations Department will discuss with the course the possibility of moving relevant fixtures to a date more suited to the weather conditions and soil type of the course. The BHA Racing Department will then be advised accordingly.

Where additional fixtures are made available, the BHA Racing Department will consult with the Racecourse and Racecourse Operations Department (including the Inspectors of Courses) to understand and take into account any impact on the racing surface in the decision-mailing process.

Groundsperson

8At least two individuals of the Groundstaff team (which includes the Clerk of the Course) must be qualified in turf management (agriculture or, preferably, amenity horticulture) to the following levels or equivalent:

(i)One member of the Groundstaff Team: Based on NVQ Level 3/Racecourse Groundstaff Management Skills Course

(ii)Second member of the Groundstaff Team: Based on NVQ Level 2/Racecourse Groundstaff Turf Husbandry Skills Course.

Existing Clerks of the Course and Head Groundsperson in place before 1 January 1999 are exempted from the qualification requirement on the basis of their previous experience.

Note: Any newly appointed Head Grounds person must be qualified in both elements (i) and (ii) above within 12 months of being employed in the role.

Preparation of the Ground – Turf Courses

9Equipment

The Managing Executive must apply best management practices and have access to the following maintenance equipment as a minimum:

(i)suitable tractors with low ground pressu re/turf tyres to minimise the risk of damage to the racing surface . The tractor must have 3 point linkage and external spool values;

(ii)front-mounted rotary or cylinder mower(s) , unless perm ission has been granted by the Inspector of C ourses for the use of rear - mounted mowers on the racing surface;

(iii)Tractor mounted sports surface spiker/slitter with a minimum depth of tine of 150mm;

(iv)Tractor mounted aerator with heave. Approval must be gained from the Racecourse Operations Department for other types of aeration equipment;

(v)Tractor mounted fertiliser spreader;

(vi)Tractor mounted light ring rollers;

(vii)Tractor mounted grassland harrows or similar;

(viii)Tractor mounted spraying equipment (all spraying equipment must conform to current Pesticide Legislation);

(ix)Tractor mounted overseeder/direct drill;

(x)Tractor mounted top dresser.

Managing Executives may use a sport surface contractor for occasional specialist work to the racing surface but must ensure that contractors are issued with clear instructions on what equipment is acceptable for use and the practices to be adopted in accordance with those defined in this Instruction (i.e. low ground pressure tyres etc).

10Irrigation

To achieve a consistent racing surface when there is a risk of the ground drying out, racecourses must have the ability to apply a minimum of 6mm of water in 24 hours. Where a racecourse installs a completely new irrigation system, the system and supply must enable the ability to apply 12mm of water in 24hours. All racecourses staging Jump fixtures during May - September must also have the ability to apply 12mm of water in 24 hours.

Furthermore, to ensure consistency and efficiency of water applications can be maintained at all times, racecourses must have access to a back up pump system so that the means of application is not impaired.

11Putting Ground Back After Racing

The ground must be reinstated as soon as possible after racing to optimise sward recovery. Guidelines on the most suitable method for reinstating the ground are described in Annex A.

Preparation of the Surface – All Weather Courses

12Equipment

The Managing Executive must apply best management practices and have access to the following maintenance equipment as a minimum:

(i)suitable tractors with tyres appropriate for the equipment in use;

(ii)gallopmaster with wheel eradicators (if appropriate);

(iii)power harrow; BHAGI 3.2 Dtd 28 March 2026

(iv)disc harrow;

(v)chain harrow;

(vi)flat roll;

(vii)ring roll;

(viii)grader;

(ix)rotovator.

Drainage and Other Work Involving the Displacement of the Racing Surface

Notification of Works

13Where work which has to be carried out in an emergency situation is involved, a report should be made to the Racecourse Operations Department within 48 hours after the work has been done. In all other situations, including displacement of the racing surface, a request for approval must be made to the Racecourse Operations Department well in advance of the anticipated commencement of work.

Notes:

(i)The Racecourse Operations Department will subsequently notify the relevant Inspector of Courses of the report or request.
